issues.description: The problem statement UML declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as type double, but the reference solution defines these attributes as int. This mismatch can confuse students about which numeric type to use when implementing the class and may cause tests or the provided solution to disagree with student code if they follow the UML literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the attribute types across artifacts. Either update the UML and problem statement to use int for numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents (to match the solution and typical student expectations), or change the solution and tests to use double consistently for those attributes and adjust related methods accordingly.

issues.description: Within the problem statement UML the two student-count attributes are typed as double while getTotalNumberOfStudents() is declared to return int. This internal inconsistency in the specification (double attributes vs an int-returning total) creates ambiguity about expected behavior (e.g., rounding/casting) when students implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification internally consistent: either change the two student-count attributes in the UML to int (so getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int is consistent), or change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return double (and update the solution/tests) if fractional counts are intended. Prefer using int for student counts unless a fractional value is explicitly required.
